subtitle: When Ming Sails Met Malabar Pepper

panels.shot: epic wide of Zheng He’s flagship approaching a crowded Calicut harbor at sunset
panels.action: Zheng He stands on the high stern of a massive Ming warship, Ma Huan beside him with a scroll, as the pepper-laden shore of Calicut glows before a forest of masts.

dialogue.text: In the fifteenth century, Zheng He and Ma Huan carried Ming China’s gaze to Calicut—where a pepper port, not a battlefield, became the bridge between two worlds.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी में झेंग हे और मा हुआन ने मिंग चीन की नज़र कलिकट तक पहुँचा दी—जहाँ जंग नहीं, मिर्च का बंदरगाह दो दुनिया के बीच पुल बना।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Zheng He’s weathered face looking over charts in Nanjing
panels.action: In a hall near the Yangtze, Zheng He studies sea charts on a low table, Ma Huan kneeling nearby with brushes and paper, carved model ships and compasses between them.

dialogue.text: From Nanjing, Yongle’s admiral Zheng He was ordered to the western oceans, to make distant rulers know the Ming throne by name.

i18n.hi: नानजिंग से योंगले के अमीरल झेंग हे को हुक्म मिला—पश्चिमी समंदरों में जा कर दूर के बादशाहों को मिंग सिंहासन का नाम बताओ।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over a crowded Ming shipyard on the Yangtze delta
panels.action: Rows of large wooden hulls sit in a bustling shipyard, workers hauling timbers and rigging, Zheng He and Ma Huan walking along a ramp, dwarfed by the rising fleet.

dialogue.text: Shipyards thundered along the Yangtze. The treasure fleets rose—large, ocean-going junks whose exact size later scholars would debate, but whose reach no one doubted.

i18n.hi: यांग्त्सी किनारे शिपयार्ड गरजे। ख़ज़ाने से लदे बेड़े उठे—बड़े, समंदर पार जाने वाले जंक्स, जिनका सही आकार विद्वान बहस करते हैं, पर पहुँच पर किसी को शक नहीं था।

panels.shot: wide shot at sea of a Ming squadron under full sail on rolling swells
panels.action: Multiple Ming ships cut across deep blue waters under layered sails, crew moving along decks; Zheng He and Ma Huan stand near the rail, watching the sky and waves.

dialogue.text: Crossing the Bay of Bengal, Zheng He’s squadron headed for a new name on the Ming horizon—Kalikut, the pepper port Ma Huan would later praise in his Yingya Shenglan.

i18n.hi: बंगाल की खाड़ी पार कर झेंग हे का बेड़ा मिंग के नए निशाने की ओर चला—कलिकुट, वो मिर्च बंदरगाह जिसे मा हुआन बाद में ‘इंग्या शेंगलान’ में सराहेगा।

panels.shot: sweeping wide of Calicut harbor from offshore, showing cosmopolitan crowd
panels.action: The ships approach Calicut’s shore, where smaller dhows and canoes swarm; warehouses face the sea, and traders from many lands mingle along the busy waterfront.

dialogue.text: Calicut’s beach was already a world street—Arab, Indian, Southeast Asian traders sharing a harbor ruled by the Zamorin, whose power rested on spice and safe anchorage.

i18n.hi: कलिकट की रेत खुद एक दुनिया की गली थी—अरब, भारतीय, दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई व्यापारी, सब उस ज़मोरिन के बंदरगाह में जिसे मसालों और सुरक्षित लंगर से ताक़त मिलती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind as Zheng He descends to a decorated reception pavilion
panels.action: Under palm shade near the shore, local officials in fine cloth wait in a pavilion; Zheng He, in Ming court robes, walks forward with calm dignity, Ma Huan a step behind with notes.

dialogue.text: When the Ming envoys stepped ashore, they did not speak of conquest. They carried lacquer, silk and words of imperial favor, expecting ritual recognition, not rule.

i18n.hi: जब मिंग के दूत किनारे उतरे, उन्होंने फतह की बात नहीं की। वो रँगदार लाख, रेशम और शाही मेहर की बातें लाए थे—रिवाज़ी मान-सम्मान माँगे, राज नहीं।

panels.shot: intimate medium inside a hall, Ming envoys facing the Zamorin
panels.action: Within a simple but dignified hall, a bejeweled Zamorin sits on a low throne, courtiers around him; Zheng He bows, holding a scroll case, Ma Huan watches, brush poised.

dialogue.speaker: zheng_he_and_ma_huan
dialogue.text: From the Son of Heaven in China, greetings to the lord of Kalikut.

i18n.hi: चीन के स्वर्ग-पुत्र की तरफ़ से, कलिकुट के स्वामी को सलाम।

panels.shot: close-up on Ma Huan’s hand writing in a travelogue by lamplight
panels.action: That night, Ma Huan sits cross-legged in a modest room, lit by an oil lamp, carefully writing characters on paper, his expression intent as he recalls the day’s sights.

dialogue.text: Later, Ma Huan’s brush caught what his eyes had seen—Calicut’s ruler, its markets, its weights, its pepper and customs—turning a day’s diplomacy into lasting record.

i18n.hi: बाद में, मा हुआन की कलम ने वो सब पकड़ लिया जो आँखों ने देखा था—कलिकट का शासक, बाज़ार, बाट-तौल, मिर्च और रीति-रिवाज़—एक दिन की सियासत को स्थायी दर्ज बना दिया।

panels.shot: busy market wide in Calicut with Ma Huan observing
panels.action: In a crowded bazaar near the shore, pepper sacks, textiles and metal goods are piled high; Ma Huan stands slightly apart, watching sellers weigh pepper on balances.

dialogue.text: He noted the pepper weighed on scales, the money used, the mingling of faiths and tongues—all details that would later show Ming readers how this Malabar port worked.

i18n.hi: उसने लिखा कैसे मिर्च तराज़ू पर तौली जाती है, कैसा पैसा चलता है, कैसे मज़हब और ज़बानें घुलती-मिलती हैं—वो सारी बातें जो मिंग के पाठकों को बताती थीं कि ये मलाबार बंदरगाह कैसे चलता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Zheng He and the Zamorin exchanging gifts in the hall
panels.action: Zheng He presents fine silk and porcelain on trays; the Zamorin’s attendants bring spices and local goods in return, both sides composed, the hall marked by mutual formality.

dialogue.text: The Zamorin accepted Chinese gifts and sent his own. In Ming language this was tribute, yet in Calicut it was a way to anchor new prestige in a long web of sea trade.

i18n.hi: ज़मोरिन ने चीनी तोहफ़े कबूल किए और अपने भेजे। मिंग की ज़बान में ये ‘खिराज’ था, मगर कलिकट में ये समंदरों की पुरानी जाल में नई इज़्ज़त का लंगर था।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Ming ships departing Calicut under calm skies
panels.action: The Ming fleet slowly pulls away from Calicut’s shore, smaller boats escorting them; Zheng He stands at the rail looking back, while Ma Huan gazes ahead, thoughtful.

dialogue.text: The ships did not stay to rule. They left behind impressions and promises, then turned east, carrying news of Calicut to the court chronicles and the port lists of China.

i18n.hi: जहाज़ राज करने नहीं रुके। वो छापें और वादे छोड़ कर लौट गए, पूर्व की ओर मुड़े, कलिकट की ख़बर चीन के दरबार के इतिहास और बंदरगाह सूचियों में ले गए।

panels.shot: solemn interior shot of a stone tablet being carved in Changle, Fujian
panels.action: Years later in Fujian, artisans carve Chinese characters into a tall stone stele, craftsmen focused; in the background, officials oversee, scrolls rolled beside them.

dialogue.text: In 1431, a stone was raised at Changle. Among the places named on that tablet was Calicut—proof carved in rock that the Ming voyages had reached this Malabar shore.

i18n.hi: १४३१ में चांगले में पत्थर का स्तंभ खड़ा हुआ। जिस तख्ती पर नाम खुदे, उनमें कलिकट भी था—पत्थर में जमा सबूत कि मिंग के सफ़र इस मलाबार तट तक पहुँचे थे।

panels.shot: close-up of the inscription surface, with ‘Kalikut’ characters being chiseled
panels.action: A chisel touches the stone, carving neat characters that spell the name of Calicut in Chinese script, chips falling, the inscription filling with carefully ordered place-names.

dialogue.text: To list a port on such a stele was to fix it in Ming memory. Calicut’s name stood beside other western-ocean harbors, a partner on paper if not a subject in fact.

i18n.hi: ऐसी शिला पर किसी बंदरगाह को लिखना, उसे मिंग की याद में गाड़ देना था। कलिकट का नाम पश्चिमी-समंदर के दूसरे बंदरगाहों के साथ खड़ा था—कागज़ पर साथी, भले हक़ में नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot in an archive-like hall where officials consult Ming Shilu
panels.action: In a grand hall, Ming officials in court robes unroll a long imperial record; the scroll shows columns of neat characters, one pointing calmly at a line mentioning Calicut.

dialogue.text: Entries in the Ming Shilu recorded missions to Calicut. The Zamorin’s envoys, the exchange of gifts, the safe passage of ships—all noted as part of an ordered world of seas.

i18n.hi: मिंग शीलू की इंदराजों में कलिकट के मिशन दर्ज थे। ज़मोरिन के दूत, तोहफ़ों का लेन-देन, जहाज़ों की सुरक्षित रवानगी—सब कुछ एक तरतीबदार समुंदर-दुनिया का हिस्सा मान कर लिखा गया।

panels.shot: reflective shot of Ma Huan in later years reading his own manuscript
panels.action: An older Ma Huan sits indoors, unrolling the Yingya Shenglan manuscript, eyes resting on the section describing Calicut, his face lit by soft daylight from a lattice window.

dialogue.text: By around 1451, Ma Huan’s Yingya Shenglan was complete. In its pages, his careful words on Calicut offered future readers a glimpse of Malabar life before new cannon arrived.

i18n.hi: करीब १४५१ तक मा हुआन की ‘इंग्या शेंगलान’ पूरी हो चुकी थी। उसकी पन्नों में कलिकट पर किए उसके लिखे ने आने वाले पाठकों को वो मलाबार दिखाया, जब नए तोप अभी पहुँचे नहीं थे।

panels.shot: wide temporal contrast shot: quiet Calicut shore in 15th century with faint ghostly outline of future European ships in the sky
panels.action: Calicut’s calm palm-lined shore fills the frame, small trading craft at anchor and warehouses behind, while in the hazy sky above, faint silhouettes of large European-style ships loom like a distant future.

dialogue.text: Soon after, Portuguese cannon would challenge the Zamorin’s harbor. Zheng He’s visits, however, had marked Calicut not with fire, but with mention—its name carried back across oceans.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही समय बाद, पुर्तगाली तोपें ज़मोरिन के बंदरगाह को ललकारेंगी। मगर झेंग हे की यात्राओं ने कलिकट को आग से नहीं, ज़िक्र से चिन्हित किया—उसका नाम समंदर पार चीन तक पहुँचा दिया।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of the Indian Ocean linking Calicut and China at sunrise
panels.action: At dawn, the Indian Ocean stretches from a silhouetted Calicut shoreline toward the horizon, where an outline of Ming ships fades into light, suggesting an invisible route between coasts.

dialogue.text: In stone, in scrolls, in Ma Huan’s travelogue, Calicut became a named address in Ming eyes—a reminder that diplomacy and record can bind distant shores long before empire and war.

i18n.hi: पत्थर में, परचों में, मा हुआन की यात्रा-कथा में, कलिकट मिंग की आँखों में एक दर्ज पते की तरह उभरा—याद दिलाते हुए कि सियासत और लिखत, साम्राज्य और जंग से बहुत पहले दूर किनारों को बाँध सकती हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Ming Sails Met Malabar Pepper
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब मिंग के जहाज़ मिले मलाबार की काली मिर्च से
